title: MS Excel
summary: Spreadsheet structure, cell references, functions, formula errors, charts and shortcuts. Excel gives the most 'compute-the-answer' questions in CKT - COUNT/IF/VLOOKP outputs are verifiable, so marks are safe.

subtopics.title: Workbook, cells and references
subtopics.concept:
**Excel** is a spreadsheet program: data goes into **cells** at the crossing of rows and columns. A file = **workbook**; each tab = **worksheet**.

**Dimensions (Excel 2007 onwards):** rows **10,48,576** (2^20, numbered 1...1048576) x columns **16,384** (2^14, named A...XFD) = 17,17,98,86,928 cells per sheet. (Excel 2003 and earlier: 65,536 x 256, last column IV.)

**References:** a cell address = column letter + row number (C5). A range = top-left:bottom-right (A1:B5 covers 2 columns x 3 rows = 6 cells).

| Reference type | Form | What happens when copied |
|---|---|---|
| Relative | A1 | Row/column shift with the formula |
| Absolute | $A$1 | Fully locked |
| Mixed | $A1 or A$1 | Column locked, or row locked |

**F4** cycles A1 -> $A$1 -> A$1 -> $A1 while editing. Cross-sheet reference: Sheet2!B4; cross-workbook adds [Book1] before the sheet name. The **Name Box** (left of formula bar) shows/renames the active cell; the **formula bar** shows the cell's real content. The **fill handle** (small square at the active cell's corner) copies formulas or extends series (AutoFill). Formulas always begin with **=**.

tricks.title: Dollar locks
tricks.body: A **$** before the letter locks the column; before the number locks the row. $A$1 = both locked ('dollar = padlock'). F4 taps through the four states.

example.q: Which reference keeps the row fixed but lets the column change?

mistakes: Saying Excel 2019 has 65,536 rows - that ended with Excel 2003.
Writing a range as A1-B5; the separator is a colon (A1:B5).
Forgetting that F4 toggles references only while editing a formula (outside editing it repeats the last action).

subtopics.title: Functions you must know
subtopics.concept:
| Category | Functions |
|---|---|
| Maths | SUM, SUMIF, PRODUCT, ROUND, INT, MOD, ABS, POWER, SQRT |
| Statistics | AVERAGE, COUNT, COUNTA, COUNTBLANK, COUNTIF, MAX, MIN, MEDIAN, MODE, RANK, LARGE, SMALL, STDEV |
| Logical | IF, AND, OR, NOT, IFS, IFERROR |
| Text | LEN, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, CONCATENATE/CONCAT, TRIM, UPPER, LOWER, PROPER |
| Date-time | TODAY, NOW, DAY, MONTH, YEAR, DATEDIF |
| Lookup | VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH, XLOOKUP (2021+) |
| Financial | PMT (loan instalment), FV, PV, NPV |

**Count-family (classic trap):** COUNT counts **numeric cells only**; COUNTA counts all **non-empty** cells; COUNTBLANK counts empty cells; COUNTIF counts cells meeting a condition (e.g. COUNTIF(A1:A10,">80")).

**Lookup:** VLOOKUP(value, table, col_index, FALSE) searches the **first column** of the table **vertically** and returns the matching row's col_index-th column; FALSE = exact match. HLOOKUP works horizontally on the first row.

**Text/date:** LEN counts characters (LEN("SSCCGL") = 6); TRIM strips extra spaces; PROPER capitalises Each Word; UPPER/LOWER change case. TODAY() gives today's date (updates); NOW() gives date **and time**.

tricks.title: COUNT counts Numbers, COUNTA counts Anything
tricks.body: COUNT = digits only; COUNTA = everything non-empty (text too); COUNTBLANK = the gaps. Test any MCQ by tagging each cell in the range N (number), T (text), E (empty).

example.q: Range has 3 numbers, 1 text cell, 1 blank. COUNT? COUNTA?

tricks.title: V of VLOOKUP = Vertical
tricks.body: VLOOKUP hunts down the **first column**; HLOOKUP along the **first row**. The 4th argument FALSE = exact match ('F for Full match').

example.q: VLOOKUP searches the table for the lookup value in which direction?

tricks.title: TODAY vs NOW
tricks.body: **TODAY()** = date only; **NOW()** = date + time. Both refresh on recalculation (unlike Ctrl+; which stamps a fixed date).

example.q: Function returning current date and time together?

mistakes: Letting COUNT count text cells - it skips them silently.
Looking up VLOOKUP values in any column - the lookup value must be in the table's first column.
Believing TODAY() freezes the date - it recalculates; Ctrl+; stamps a static date.

subtopics.title: Formula errors, charts and data tools
subtopics.concept:
**Error messages:**

| Error | Cause |
|---|---|
| #DIV/0! | Division by zero or by an empty cell |
| #NAME? | Text Excel cannot recognise (misspelt function/name) |
| #VALUE! | Wrong data type in the formula (text where a number is needed) |
| #REF! | Invalid cell reference (referenced cells deleted) |
| #N/A | Lookup value not found |
| #NUM! | Bad numeric argument (e.g. SQRT of a negative) |
| ###### | Column too narrow - a display issue, NOT an error |
| Circular Reference warning | Formula refers back to its own cell |

**Charts:** Column - compare categories; **Line - trends over time**; **Pie - parts of one whole**; Bar - horizontal comparison; Area - cumulative trend; Scatter - relationship between two variables. Alt+F1 inserts a default chart on the sheet; F11 puts it on a new chart sheet.

**Data tools:** Sort (multi-level), Filter/AutoFilter (**Ctrl+Shift+L**), Conditional Formatting (colour scales, icon sets), Data Validation (dropdowns/limits), **Pivot Table** (drag-and-drop summary of big data), What-If Analysis - **Goal Seek** (find the input that produces a wanted output), Scenario Manager, Data Table. **Freeze Panes** locks rows/columns on screen; Wrap Text shows long text on multiple lines; Merge & Center combines cells; Sheet protection locks cells against edits; **Sparklines** are tiny in-cell charts.

tricks.title: ###### is not an error
tricks.body: Widen the column - done. Real errors start with #: DIV/0 (zero), NAME (spelling), VALUE (type), REF (deleted), N/A (not found). Match the cause table above.

example.q: A cell shows #####. The problem is?
example.solution: Column width, not a formula error.

tricks.title: Chart chooser
tricks.body: **Pie = Parts, Line = Line of time (trend), Column = Compare, Scatter = relationship.** 'Trend over months' questions always end at Line.

example.q: Best chart for monthly sales trend?

tricks.title: Goal Seek direction
tricks.body: Goal Seek: you give the **answer**, it finds the **input**. Pivot Table: you give the **data**, it gives summaries.

example.q: Which tool finds the marks needed in the last test to average exactly 80?

mistakes: Calling ##### an error - it is only a narrow column.
Using a pie chart for a time trend - pies show one whole's shares at one point.
Saying #REF! appears for misspelt functions - that is #NAME?.

subtopics.title: Excel shortcuts and file facts
subtopics.concept:
| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Insert current date / time | Ctrl+; / Ctrl+Shift+; |
| AutoSum | Alt+= |
| Edit active cell | F2 |
| Toggle $ references | F4 (while editing) |
| Format Cells dialog | Ctrl+1 |
| Fill down / right | Ctrl+D / Ctrl+R |
| Select column / row | Ctrl+Space / Shift+Space |
| Insert new worksheet | Shift+F11 |
| Chart on new sheet | F11 |
| Next / previous sheet | Ctrl+PgDn / Ctrl+PgUp |
| New line inside a cell | Alt+Enter |
| Toggle filters | Ctrl+Shift+L |
| Show formulas instead of results | Ctrl+` |
| Hide rows | Ctrl+9 (restore Ctrl+Shift+9) |
| Spell check | F7 |
| Create Table | Ctrl+T |
| Percent / currency / date format | Ctrl+Shift+% / $ / # |

**File facts:** default extension .xlsx from Excel 2007 (before: .xls); macro workbook .xlsm; template .xltx; CSV .csv; OpenDocument .ods. Default chart is a Clustered Column. A quick printed grid = Page Layout view / Page Break Preview.

tricks.title: Date stamp duo
tricks.body: **Ctrl+; = date, Ctrl+Shift+; = time** - the Shift makes it work-o'clock (time). 'Current date in a cell' questions answer Ctrl+;.

example.q: Shortcut to insert today's date in a cell?

tricks.title: F-key row for Excel
tricks.body: F2 edit, F4 lock, F7 spell, F9 recalc, F11 chart sheet, F12 Save As - the F-row reads like Excel's toolbar.

example.q: Shortcut to create a chart on a new sheet?

tricks.title: Alt+= = AutoSum
tricks.body: Alt with the plus key writes =SUM() over the adjacent numbers instantly - the fastest marks in the section.

mistakes: Giving Ctrl+D for date - Ctrl+D fills down; the date stamp is Ctrl+;.
Saying F4 always toggles references - only while a reference is being edited; otherwise F4 repeats the last action.
Answering .xls for Excel 2016 files - .xls is 97-2003; the default is .xlsx.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: '=COUNT(A1:A5) returns?' with a small data table - a mini computation, not recall.
pyqPatterns.approach: Replicate the function mentally (or on paper): tag cells number/text/blank for COUNT family; evaluate the condition for IF; sum/average directly.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which shortcut inserts the current date in a cell?'
pyqPatterns.approach: Ctrl+; date, Alt+= AutoSum, F2 edit, Shift+F11 sheet, F4 lock - keep the F-row and Ctrl-row drilled.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which error appears when a formula divides by an empty cell?'
pyqPatterns.approach: Match cause -> code: zero/blank divide = #DIV/0!, unknown text = #NAME?, type mismatch = #VALUE!, deleted ref = #REF!, not found = #N/A, narrow column = ##### (not an error).

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which chart best shows the trend of monthly rainfall?'
pyqPatterns.approach: Pie = parts of a whole, Line = trend over time, Column/Bar = compare categories, Scatter = two-variable relationship.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'A formula with $A$1 copied down to the next row will?'
pyqPatterns.approach: $-locked parts stay put; unlocked parts shift with the formula's new position.

solvedExamples.q: Cells A1:A5 contain: 72, Fail, 85, (blank), 90. What does =COUNT(A1:A5) return?
solvedExamples.solution: COUNT counts only numeric cells: 72, 85 and 90 -> 3. The text 'Fail' and the empty cell are ignored (COUNTA would have returned 4).
solvedExamples.shortcut: COUNT = numbers only. Tag each cell N/T/E and count the Ns.

solvedExamples.q: Cell A1 contains 72. The formula =IF(A1>50,"Pass","Fail") displays:
solvedExamples.solution: The condition 72>50 is TRUE, so IF returns its second argument, the text Pass. (If A1 held 40, the third argument Fail would show.)
solvedExamples.shortcut: Evaluate the condition first; return argument 2 on TRUE, argument 3 on FALSE. Plain TRUE/FALSE only appear from a bare comparison like =A1>50.

solvedExamples.q: B1 contains the formula =$A$1*2 and is copied to B2. B2 will contain:
solvedExamples.solution: $A$1 is fully absolute, so the copied formula is unchanged: =$A$1*2. Only relative parts (like A1) would shift row-wise on copying.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Dollar = padlock. $A$1 never moves; A1 becomes A2 on a one-row copy.

solvedExamples.q: Which error results from =A1/B1 when B1 is empty?
solvedExamples.solution: An empty cell is treated as zero, so the formula divides by zero and Excel shows #DIV/0!. #VALUE! means a wrong data type, #REF! a deleted reference, #NAME? unknown text.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Blank divisor = zero divisor = #DIV/0!. Don't be fooled into choosing #VALUE! for a blank cell.

solvedExamples.q: How many rows and columns does an Excel 2019 worksheet have?
solvedExamples.solution: Excel 2007 onwards: 2^20 = 10,48,576 rows and 2^14 = 16,384 columns (A to XFD). The 65,536 x 256 grid belongs to Excel 2003 and earlier.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Remember the pair 2^20 x 2^14; the option swapping rows with columns is the deliberate trap.

practice.q: The default file extension of a workbook created in MS Excel 2019 is:
practice.solution: Excel 2007 onwards saves workbooks as .xlsx (Office Open XML). .xls is the 97-2003 format, .xlsm is macro-enabled, .ods is OpenDocument.
practice.shortcut: X = XML = 2007+ across all Office extensions.

practice.q: In Excel, the intersection of a row and a column is called a:
practice.solution: A cell is the single box at a column-row crossing, addressed as ColumnLetter+RowNumber (e.g. B7). A range is a rectangular block of cells.
practice.shortcut: Spreadsheet atom = cell; address = letter + number.

practice.q: Cells A1:A5 contain: 72, Fail, 85, (blank), 90. What does =COUNTA(A1:A5) return?
practice.solution: COUNTA counts every non-empty cell - numbers and text alike: 72, 'Fail', 85, 90 = 4. The blank cell is the only one skipped.
practice.shortcut: COUNTA = Anything non-empty. COUNT would give 3 here.

practice.q: Which function returns the number of characters in a text string?
practice.solution: LEN("text") returns the character count, e.g. LEN("SSCCGL") = 6. There is no LENGTH function in Excel; COUNT works on numbers; CHAR returns the character for an ASCII code.
practice.shortcut: Excel's length function is LEN - no other name exists.

practice.q: Which function displays the current date that updates every time the workbook recalculates?
practice.solution: =TODAY() returns the live current date (updating on recalculation); =NOW() adds the time as well; =DATE() builds a date from given year/month/day; Ctrl+D fills down, it does not insert a date.
practice.shortcut: 'Date only, updating' -> TODAY(); 'date and time' -> NOW(); 'fixed stamp' -> Ctrl+;.

practice.q: VLOOKUP searches for the lookup value in which part of the table array?
practice.solution: VLOOKUP scans the first (leftmost) column of the table vertically and returns a value from the chosen column of the matching row. Searching along the first row is HLOOKUP.
practice.shortcut: V = Vertical = first column; H = Horizontal = first row.

practice.q: The formula =A1/B1 shows #DIV/0!. The most likely reason is:
practice.solution: #DIV/0! means the divisor (B1) is zero or blank. Text in A1 would raise #VALUE!; a narrow column shows #####; a misspelt function shows #NAME?.
practice.shortcut: Divide error -> look at the cell below the slash.

options: The column is too narrow to show the value
practice.solution: Excel fills the cell with # symbols when the formatted number cannot fit the column width - widen the column. It is a display condition, not an error.
practice.shortcut: Hashes = width, never an error code.

practice.q: Which chart type is best suited to show the trend of monthly sales over a year?
practice.solution: Line charts plot values across a continuous axis - ideal for time-series trends. Pie/doughnut show shares of one whole at a single point; radar compares multiple variables.
practice.shortcut: Trend over time = line, every time.

practice.q: The keyboard shortcut to insert the current date into a cell (as a fixed value) is:
practice.solution: Ctrl+; stamps today's date; Ctrl+Shift+; stamps the time; Ctrl+D fills down from the cell above; Ctrl+T creates a table.
practice.shortcut: Semicolon = stamp. Shift makes it time instead of date.

practice.q: AutoSum is applied with which shortcut?
practice.solution: Alt+= writes =SUM() over the neighbouring numeric range in one stroke. Ctrl+= applies subscript formatting in Word, not AutoSum.
practice.shortcut: Alt with the plus sign = add them up.

practice.q: Which shortcut inserts a brand-new worksheet in the workbook?
practice.solution: Shift+F11 adds a new worksheet. Ctrl+N creates a new workbook (file), and Ctrl+F11 has no default action in modern Excel.
practice.shortcut: New sheet inside the file = Shift+F11; whole new file = Ctrl+N.

practice.q: To find the input value that makes a formula produce a desired result, use:
practice.solution: Goal Seek (What-If Analysis) back-solves one input cell to hit a target output. Pivot Tables summarise data, AutoFilter hides rows, Freeze Panes locks screen areas.
practice.shortcut: You know the answer, want the input -> Goal Seek.

practice.q: The formula =SUM(A1:A5, 10) is entered in B1. A1:A5 contain 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. The result is:
practice.solution: SUM adds the range (2+4+6+8+10 = 30) plus the extra argument 10, giving 40.
practice.shortcut: SUM takes every argument: range total first, then any loose numbers.

practice.q: While editing a formula, pressing F4 on the reference A1 changes it to:
practice.solution: F4 cycles the reference through A1 -> $A$1 -> A$1 -> $A1 -> A1. The first press makes it fully absolute.
practice.shortcut: One tap of F4 = full lock ($ before both letter and number).
